transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood Solutions), Emily Zhang (NovaMarket Head of Partnerships), Carlos Mendes (NovaMarket Cloud Architect), Priya Rao (NovaMarket Security), Liam O'Connor (NovaMarket PM)

Summary: Align on integration milestones for listing Redwood as a managed inference partner in NovaMarket marketplace. Cover reference architecture options, API and billing integration points, security and compliance needs, benchmarking plan.

Topics: marketplace listing process, reference architecture, VPC/private deployment, KMS and encryption, SSO/SAML, RBAC, telemetry and billing hooks, benchmark plan.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everybody thanks for joining, we'll give a quick agenda — intro, go over RA options, then security then bench plan. um Samir will take the tech bits.
[00:18] Emily: thanks Jordan, excited to see how Redwood will fit into our marketplace. main thing for us is a clean on-ramp for customers and a clear reference arch to share with integrators.
[00:27] Samir: yeah absolutely; quick to orient, Redwood supports three deployment modes that matter here: hosted API (our public listing), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools for enterprise tenants) and Private / VPC options for customers who need network isolation. today we'll map which flows we need for NovaMarket listing.
[00:46] Carlos: quick question — for marketplace listing do you normally have customers connect to hosted API or do you do marketplace-managed Dedicated instances? we have a few large sellers that want VPC peering.
[00:58] Samir: good q. we do both. marketplace listing typically points to our hosted API for easiest onboarding; then high-value customers on NovaMarket can upgrade to Dedicated or Private. for VPC peering we support VPC-on-VPC peering and also a private control plane model for the Private deployment.
[01:18] Priya: what about key management — we need to ensure our customers' keys aren't in Redwood control plane if they choose private. can you outline KMS options?
[01:27] Samir: yes. options: 1) Redwood-held keys for hosted offerings; 2) bring-your-own-KMS via customer-managed keys (we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM partners) when in Private mode; 3) for Dedicated we can support customer-managed keys at node level. in the RA doc I'll show a key flow diagram.
[01:44] Liam: and billing — NovaMarket needs usage hooks so we can bill end-customers through the marketplace. how do you expose metering?
[01:52] Jordan: we provide metering webhooks and billable usage reports per tenant and per model. for marketplace we can surface per-route cost and token counts, and we can push events to NovaMarket via a secure webhook. we also support monthly invoice exports and CSVs for reconciliation.
[02:12] Emily: do you have a standard marketplace integration checklist? like the docs we give to partners.
[02:18] Jordan: yes, we'll share a checklist. it includes IAM roles, webhook endpoints, sample API keys, test tenant setup, reference arch diagram, certs, compliance docs. I'll attach the checklist after the call.
[02:30] Carlos: on networking — if a customer picks Private and we host in their VPC how is egress limited? any need for NAT?
[02:38] Samir: usually the control plane is out-of-band but compute runs in customer VPC; egress is controlled via customer's NAT/GW. we support VPC endpoints and private links. note: some customers prefer a fully air-gapped on-prem package; we have an on-prem appliance option too.
[02:55] Priya: security requirements — SOC2 type II ok? or do we need iso 27001? also audit logs for all inference requests, retention 1 year minimum.
[03:04] Samir: Redwood is SOC2 and ISO in progress, we can share our attestations. for audit logs we stream structured logs to the customer's S3 or logging endpoint; retention is configurable. I'll add that to the RA doc.
[03:20] [00:03:20] Carlos: can you talk about model pinning and versioning — our sellers will want to pin a model version per product listing so results are stable.
[03:28] Samir: yep, our serving runtime supports model version pinning and rollouts. we also support model variants (quantized vs fp16) and automatic fallback policies if capacity is constrained. important for marketplace: you'll want us to expose the model version and quant profile in the listing metadata.
[03:45] Emily: regarding the listing UX — we'd prefer a single API endpoint for marketplace orchestration so buyers don't manage multiple keys. is that feasible?
[03:53] Jordan: feasible — we can do a marketplace proxy route where NovaMarket mints short-lived tokens per buyer and we accept the marketplace-issued token. it's similar to how some cloud marketplaces operate. that does require webhook exchanges and an onboarding webhook from NovaMarket.
[04:10] Maya: just to add, we also support SAML/SSO SSO for console access and RBAC for team-level controls. for the marketplace we usually limit admin console access and push metering only.
[04:23] [00:04:23] Priya: any PII concerns in inference traces? we need to ensure PII is not stored for the buyer without consent.
[04:31] Samir: default is no persistent storage of prompts unless customer enables audit logging; we support redaction and field-level masking in our logging pipeline. we'll provide config flags in the RA.
[04:42] Carlos: latency / perf — can you share typical p95 numbers for 8k token context with a TGI model?
[04:50] Samir: we have p95 numbers in the benchmark doc; roughly for an 8k context model under hosted API it's around 220-400 ms per 1k tokens depending on the model and batching; for Dedicated you get lower variance. we'll run a targeted benchmark with your sample data to give precise numbers.
[05:08] Emily: great, can we see a sample reference architecture now? even a high level.
[05:14] Samir: sure — I'll describe then share. picture: marketplace front-end -> NovaMarket orchestration -> marketplace proxy (short-lived token) -> Redwood ingress (load balancer) -> routing layer (hosted vs dedicated vs private) -> serving nodes -> optional KV cache and prefix cache -> responses back. for private: control plane is NovaMarket managed tenant mapping, compute in customer VPC, KMS flow as we discussed.
[05:38] [00:05:38] Liam: do you have terraform templates or helm charts for the Private deployment?
[05:44] Samir: yes, we provide deployment templates and example helm charts for on-prem and VPC environments, and terraform for cloud provisioning. we'll include the repo link in the RA.
[05:52] Jordan: I'll put the repo link in the follow-up: https://git.redwood/partners/novamarket-integration (placeholder).
[06:00] Carlos: about data residency — some of our EU customers require data to remain in EU regions; how granular is your region control?
[06:08] Samir: we allow region pinning per-tenant and per-model. for Dedicated and Private you can force region-specific pools. hosted API also supports region routing for major regions.
[06:18] Priya: encryption in transit and at rest? certs?
[06:22] Samir: TLS for in transit, keys for at rest via KMS, node-level disk encryption supported. we can provide cert rotation docs.
[06:31] [00:06:31] Emily: any required legal artifacts for listing — indemnity, SLA?
[06:36] Jordan: for marketplace listing we generally provide a partner addendum, standard SLA for Dedicated customers, and a data processing addendum for GDPR. legal can coordinate once we get initial interest.
[06:46] Maya: ops notes: telemetry — we surface per-route token counts, per-tenant latency histograms, and error rates. NovaMarket can pull via API or subscribe to streaming metrics.
[06:58] Carlos: about the webhook for metering — what's the typical payload?
[07:02] Samir: sample events include tenant_id, route_id, tokens_consumed, model_id, timestamp, and a signature header. we'll share schema.
[07:12] [00:07:12] Liam: what about trial limits for buyers — we want to issue credits and cap per-tenant throughput. does Redwood enforce per-tenant rate limits?
[07:19] Samir: yes, per-tenant quotas and throttles are standard; rate-limit rules are configurable via the console or API.
[07:26] Emily: on the RA diagram make sure to call out where NovaMarket will be responsible vs Redwood — e.g., token billing mapping, buyer onboarding.
[07:35] Jordan: good call. we'll produce a mapping table in the RA doc.
[07:40] [00:07:40] Priya: can you confirm log delivery options? S3, syslog, SIEM connectors? we need to push to our Splunk or SIEM.
[07:49] Samir: S3, Kinesis, Pub/Sub, and direct syslog/Splunk forwarders are supported. we'll include example configurations.
[07:58] Carlos: for the benchmarking plan — want to measure latency, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens. we'll provide sample prompts and workloads.
[08:06] Samir: perfect. let's plan a 1-hour benchmark where we run 100k token batch and measure p50/p95/p99 and GPU utilization. Samir and Carlos to sync on exact test harness.
[08:18] Jordan: ok next, integration timeline — what would be the minimum time to get a hosted listing live once artifacts are ready?
[08:25] Samir: typically 2-3 weeks for hosted listing (docs, test tenant, webhook integration), Dedicated/private will be 4-8 weeks depending on network approvals and KMS setup.
[08:36] Maya: for joint solution marketing assets we can draft a reference architecture and co-branded diagram — will need approval flows.
[08:44] Emily: yes please include that; our PM wants a draft RA by end of next week.
[08:50] [00:08:50] Jordan: we'll aim to deliver the draft RA by Monday 2026-11-23.
[08:55] Priya: a compliance wrinkle — some sellers require that we do not log full prompts; can Redwood support partial redaction in logs?
[09:03] Samir: yes, field-level redaction and hashing of sensitive fields is supported; we'll show config examples.
[09:11] Carlos: small nit — are your SDKs first-class for Node/Python/Go? our integrations are mostly Node.
[09:17] Samir: Node and Python are primary, Go SDK also available. we'll share the SDK quickstart.
[09:23] [00:09:23] Emily: anything else on go-to-market?
[09:27] Jordan: not technical but we'll coordinate PR and joint blog once initial customers are onboarded.
[09:33] Liam: question — for marketplace search ranking, is there metadata we can surface like cost per 1k tokens, latency SLO, region availability?
[09:42] Samir: yes the listing metadata can include cost estimates, SLOs, region tags, and model capabilities.
[09:49] [00:09:49] Maya: wrap-up— recap of action items and owners. Jordan?
[09:54] Jordan: recap: Samir will draft RA and templates; Jordan will send marketplace checklist and pricing template; Carlos will provision test account; Priya will send compliance specifics. full next steps in calendar invite.
[10:08] Emily: great thanks all — excited to move forward.
[10:12] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and docs.

Meeting end.
